course.title: Data Science — Complete Deep Course
course.description: A Data Science-specific, beginner-to-advanced course with detailed concepts, practical analysis, dedicated tasks, validation, interpretation and a complete learning-platform capstone.
course.curriculumPolicy: Module and lesson counts are determined by the concepts required to learn the discipline properly; no fixed cross-domain template is imposed.
learningOutcomes: Clean, query, analyze or model data appropriately.

modules.title: Data Science Foundations
modules.description: Problem framing, datasets, variables, targets, features and the data-science lifecycle.

lessons.title: Data Science Foundations
lessons.description: Problem framing, datasets, variables, targets, features and the data-science lifecycle.
learningObjectives: Apply the technique to realistic learning data.

notes.text: Problem framing, datasets, variables, targets, features and the data-science lifecycle.

Learn data science foundations by connecting the concept to a real data question. First understand what the data represents, then perform the operation, validate the result, and finally explain what the result means.

Data Science Foundations is useful when turning raw learning-platform data into reliable information, decisions or predictive models. The student should understand both the technical operation and the meaning of the result.

Scenario: Frame a student-success prediction problem.

Example workflow: define the question -> inspect data -> transform/analyze -> validate -> interpret -> document limitations.

items: Check sample sizes and missing values.

lessons.description: Train/test splits, cross-validation, accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC and calibration.
learningObjectives: Apply the technique to realistic learning data.

notes.text: Train/test splits, cross-validation, accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC and calibration.

Learn model evaluation by connecting the concept to a real data question. First understand what the data represents, then perform the operation, validate the result, and finally explain what the result means.

Model Evaluation is useful when turning raw learning-platform data into reliable information, decisions or predictive models. The student should understand both the technical operation and the meaning of the result.

notes.caption: Add a teaching diagram showing the data flow for Model Evaluation.

items: Understand the shape and meaning of the data.
Interpret the result without overstating it.

notes.code:
Scenario: Evaluate a model with metrics appropriate to the business problem.

Example workflow: define the question -> inspect data -> transform/analyze -> validate -> interpret -> document limitations.

items: Check sample sizes and missing values.
State limitations before making a decision.
Using a metric without defining it.
Building a model before defining the business problem.
Reporting a number without explaining uncertainty or limitations.
I can explain Model Evaluation in my own words.
I can apply it to a small dataset.
I can identify at least one limitation.
I can explain what decision the result can and cannot support.
